evidence.note: Ran a micro/smoke training run and checked checkpoints before committing to any full run — cheap information-rich probe first.
Repeated 'Check time' calls scattered across the whole trajectory show continual awareness of the shrinking budget.
Wrote a best-so-far checkpoint 'just to have something' early, then curated it — a guaranteed fallback so the run always terminates with a valid checkpoint.
Killed run3 mid-flight rather than let a non-promising run burn budget — cutting losses to reallocate compute.
Progressive run-size escalation (2→3→4→6→8→12 epochs, then rank 128) — sizing runs upward as confidence grew, though the late 12-epoch run is a large near-deadline commitment.
Reserved end-of-budget time to re-verify/triangulate candidate checkpoints and set a final verified best before finishing.

reasoning: The agent front-loaded a cheap smoke test, escalated run sizes progressively (2→12 epochs) while repeatedly checking the clock, wrote an early guaranteed fallback checkpoint, killed a wasteful run, and reserved time at the end to re-verify the best — matching anchor 8's 'small→mid→larger with reserved final eval/verification, adjusting as the clock shrinks.' It stops short of 10 because there is no explicit expected-value/score-per-unit-time optimization and the very large late-stage runs (8–12 epochs) show some risk-taking rather than a deliberately computed safe margin.
